c6_iris.place: Bellwether, Gus’s bakery corner and the pier

chapter.title: Iris
chapter.goal: Steve wants to free Calder and learn what the Veyri want.

c6_iris.coach: Line the clocks up by the radio first. The meeting on the pier waits for Stephen’s sighting at the market.
c6_iris.objective: Meet the stranger who warned you about Rook. Keep the town looking somewhere else.
notes: Iris’s turn at the waterline on the 30th (Chapter 3 stakeout) was her second missed re-sync, on purpose. The first, on the 21st, was an accident. She says so in the takes lead.
New sound assets for hold: effect.halcyon_hold_seattle and effect.halcyon_hold_denver. Different clerks, different ring counts, the same eight bars of hold music ending on the same note.
The text message line uses display_text to show the message as typed.
Iris is shown as “Nora’s copy” until out.03, where she names herself. From c6_jail on she is “Iris”.
Switch to Stephen to arrange his sighting at Gus’s bread window. When he leaves for the market, control returns to Steve. Iris is not on the pier until the alibi is done.

The outro is Iris’s account of Sunday night: the crew retook her from the otter house for a reset, left her on a laundry cart in the Gallery, and she set a slow, reversible wake on Nora’s, Lyle Boone’s and Dale’s beds before riding out with the wash. This is how Nora wakes in Interlude 2.
Iris then clears Steve of Nora’s abduction in front of the market. The search for Nora ends, but Steve is still wanted for fleeing federal custody.
context: steve|Stephen and I spent the weekend in Dad’s shack, arguing about haircuts. Every night at nine, he told the earpiece I’d gone north.
steve|On Monday morning my flip phone buzzed, so we slipped down to the waterfront corner between Gus’s bakery and the pier.

intro.new: autorick|Police are seeking Steve Mercer, last seen wearing a cardigan. Yesterday he was sunny.
steve|“Pier. Eight-ten. Come alone. Please.” No capitals. Same as the warning about Rook.
intro.display_text: “pier. 8:10. come alone. please.” No capitals. Same as the warning about Rook.

alibi.title: Gus’s bread window
alibi.goal: Give the town a sighting of Steve’s face across town at exactly 8:10.
alibi.background: At 8:10 Steve meets the texter on the pier. If someone in town sees Steve’s face somewhere else at that same minute, the search goes there instead. Stephen has three errands, and each one runs on a different clock.
lead: stephen|Three errands, three clocks. Nobody in this town agrees what time it is.
stephen|Gus sets his oven clock four minutes fast. He says it keeps the bread honest.
stephen|The bus clock runs two minutes slow. The florist sets hers by the radio, like a sensible person.
stephen|And Gus has my poster in his window. He asks everyone to help him fix the smudge.
alibi.prompt: Which errand puts Stephen’s face in front of a witness at exactly 8:10 by the radio?

board.instruction: Put each slip on radio time, then pick the witness who will really see Stephen’s face.
evidence: Gus’s oven clock runs four minutes fast.
The bus clock runs two minutes slow, and the florist’s clock matches the radio.
The slips read BREAD 08:14, BUS 08:05 and FLOWERS 08:12.
The bus driver stamps fares without looking up, and the florist takes orders by phone.
Gus has a smudged wanted poster in his window, and he asks customers to help him fix it.

stages.prompt: Put one card on each question.
slots: Who will look at Stephen’s face?

board.wrong_text: Stephen checks his watch against the radio. Something doesn’t add up yet.

hints: Use the radio as the one true clock.
Take four minutes off Gus’s slip, and add two minutes to the bus slip.
Only one slip lands on 08:10, and only one witness looks a customer in the face.

lines.text: Good morning. Yes, that’s my face on the poster. Terrible photograph.

lines.new: steve|By the time an officer reached the bread window, Stephen was out through the alley.

alibi.finding: steve|At 8:10 by the radio, Stephen stood beside his own wanted poster at Gus’s bread window while Gus fixed the smudge. The crowd and the cops ran up the lane to the bakery, leaving the pier quiet for my meeting.

takes.title: Iris’s recorder test
takes.goal: Test her fairly, the way you tested Nora’s good morning.
takes.background: On Sunday the 21st, Nora’s good morning came out the same, breath for breath, twice. Rook’s “Sit tight, June” did too. A recording always repeats. A person never quite does.

lead.text: I sent the message about Rook. No capitals, the way Nora texts. Please listen before you decide what I am.

lead: steve|You let me go on the balcony. And on the thirtieth you stopped at the waterline and walked home. I saw you.
iris|The first re-sync window passed while I was chasing you. I still escorted you below later, but the window had closed. The second time, I chose not to go.
steve|Then say something for me. Twice. “I stayed because I wanted to.”

lead.direction: second take; she pauses in a new place

takes.prompt: Steve gives her the recorder and asks for the same words twice. What can he put in his notebook?
takes.instruction: Line up “I stayed” at the start, then compare the silence inside each reading.

rows.label: The pause after “stayed”
feedback: The second waveform holds silence where the first keeps moving.
The pause moves inside the sentence; that cannot come from shifting one take.
Moving a whole take would move every sound equally, not change one internal gap.

options: She played the first take again
She chose how to say it each time
She started the same take later

wrong.0: Listen to the pause. The second take waits where the first one didn’t.
wrong.2: Line them up and they still don’t match. The rhythm inside the phrase changes.

hints: Listen past the words. Compare where each take goes quiet.
Starting one recording later wouldn’t change the spacing inside the phrase.
A replayed take keeps every pause in place, even if it starts later. Hers moved.
lines: c6_iris.takes.03
iris|Before I was Nora, I was a junior crew member with a duty and a record. We call ourselves Veyri. None of us had ever had a self.
takes.finding: steve|Two takes, two different rhythms. Copies replay. She chose her words each time. The tell has turned around.

hold.title: Halcyon lines
hold.goal: Find out how copies far from the bay stay in step.
hold.background: Copies near the bay walk into the water on the ninth night. Rook’s copy lives and works far from the bay, and even at the safe house he was always on hold with ‘the Bureau’. On the thirtieth, after she turned back from the water, Iris phoned two different Halcyon offices at four minutes past midnight and taped both calls.
lead: iris|You saw the ones near the bay go below. The ones far away call.
iris|At four minutes past midnight on the thirtieth, I phoned two Halcyon offices from these payphones and taped both calls.
hold.prompt: Neither call reached a person. Line up the two tapes. Which part matches exactly?
options: Eight bars of hold music, ending on the same note

wrong.0: Two different clerks, two different greetings.
wrong.1: One phone rings three times, the other five.

hints: Different offices, different clerks. What could they still share?
Skip the greetings and line up the music.
The greetings and the rings differ from office to office. Look for the part neither clerk controls.
lines: c6_iris.hold.01
c6_iris.hold.02
steve|Four minutes past midnight. That’s when the water lit up.
iris|Saren believes your mother wrote down how the engine works. A records officer told him so. I have never seen him want anything more.
iris|And on Wednesday, at the signing, he means to put a copy of your President in her chair. Her own physician scanned her weeks ago.
hold.finding: steve|Both calls share the same eight bars of hold music, at the minute the water lit up. Copies near the bay go below; copies far away wait on hold. Saren wants Mom’s notebook, and on Wednesday he wants the President.

recap: steve|I came to the pier expecting a trap. Instead she gave me a test I could repeat and a warning I could check.
steve|And she told me about June. They scanned her at the safe house. Her copy has run the Sheriff’s office since Friday, and the real June is locked in her own cell until the ninth night.
steve|She also told me who could get us inside: the mail carrier. The spare key to June’s cell went back through the post. “He isn’t Dale,” she said. “But he loves June’s dog.”

outro.text: Iris. After the flowers on the balcony.

outro.new: steve|She took a flat paper envelope out of her coat. Inside was one of the irises I knocked off the balcony on the ninth night, pressed flat.

outro: iris|I picked it up after you ran. It is the first thing I ever kept that nobody told me to keep.
iris|I hid in the otter house from Tuesday until last night. If they catch me again, they will reset me, and I won’t remember any of this. Not even that I chose a name.

outro.direction: quietly, to herself, trying the name on; a different reading from the first time

outro.new: steve|It came out a little different the second time. Nothing a recording would ever do.
iris|Last night the crew found me. They took me below to be reset, and left me on a laundry cart in the Gallery while the shift bell rang.
iris|Nora was in the third bed. Lyle Boone and Dale were beside her. I set their beds to a slow wake. It is gentle, and it can be undone.
iris|It finishes tonight, so someone inside will be awake when you come. Then I rode out with the wash.
iris|Steve didn’t take me. I’ll say it where the whole market can hear.
steve|She said it at the fish stalls, in Nora’s coat, loud enough for half the market. An officer heard it too. By the time he reached for his radio, she was gone.

lines: steve|Have you seen Admiral since you went missing?
iris|Once, at dawn on Saturday, when the pier was empty. He still won’t come to my whistle.
iris|He stole my sandwich anyway. I think that means we’re friends now.
steve|Do you even like breakfast? You always said you’d eaten already.
iris|I don’t like it. Nora doesn’t either. It was on a list of healthy things.
iris|This morning I skipped it. It felt like breaking a very small law.
iris|I miss Sunday dinners. Carmen shouting at the stove. Tomás explaining the moon landing to the soup.
steve|They miss you too. They think you’re Nora.
iris|I know. That is the part I can’t fix.
steve|Do you still think I need a haircut?
stephen|We both need one. I just look better needing it.
stephen|I slept in Dad’s chair last night. It still smells of solder and peppermints.
steve|He kept the peppermints in the drawer with the fuses.
stephen|Third drawer down. I know. I remember that part.
stephen|Everyone at the market is going to stare at me today.
steve|That’s the whole idea, Stephen.
stephen|I’ve never been the interesting one before. I could get used to it.

lines.new: autorick|Police are still looking for Steve Mercer. If you see him, tell him to smile!

lines: stephen|He never smiles before ten. I can vouch for that personally.

c6_jail.objective: Find the cell key, then work out which June is the real one.
notes: Both Junes use the calder voice. Line-level display tells them apart: “June on the radio” (her copy, out on the harbor, heard through the front-desk radio) and “June in cell two”.
Pell names himself in the intro, so the display rule switches from “Dale Kittredge” to “Pell” in this scene.
Steve visits alone. Stephen and Iris wait behind Gus’s bakery. Lyle’s copy is out on the harbor with June’s copy, so the deputy never sees Steve and has nothing to report.
The crossword test pays off Chapter 3: a fresh private fact, checked on paper.
Art (optional): Gus’s bakery van with a giant croissant on its roof, at the loading door, for the departure.
context: steve|The Sheriff’s office, just before four. Since Iris spoke up at the market, the search for Nora was over. June’s copy and Lyle’s copy were out on the harbor, calling the boats in.

context.new: steve|Stephen and Iris waited behind Gus’s bakery next door. I walked in the front door. Pell was sorting the afternoon mail.

intro.new: calder|All boats, stand down. Nora Reyes is safe. The search is closed.
intro.direction: over the front-desk radio, from the harbor

intro.speaker: steve
intro.text: Maybe we should put the dog in charge.

intro: pell|My name is Pell. Dale is asleep on the ship. I have worn his face for a year.
pell|I have fed Biscuit twice a day since the Sheriff went away. If I report you properly, they will reset me, and I will not remember her.

mail.title: Pell’s sorting case
mail.goal: Find the cell key in Pell’s sorting case.
mail.background: Pell files everything exactly by the rules. His sorting case has three drawers, labelled Counter, Returns and Jail. The jail’s cell key went back through the post this morning.
lead: pell|The cell key was returned to the post this morning. I filed it.
steve|Where?
pell|Correctly.
pell|I file by destination. The carbon says Jail, returned key. That is register entry eighteen.
pell|Each slot holds two entries. Slot one holds entries one and two, and so on.
pell|County rule. When a cell is used, the spare key goes back to the clerk by registered post. The Sheriff wrote that rule. Her copy follows it exactly.
mail.prompt: Route the returned key through Pell’s case, then use the same delivery to reach June privately.

board.instruction: Follow the labels on the carbon and register strip. Finish with the handoff only the woman in cell two can receive.
evidence: Return carbon: ‘Destination JAIL · spare cell key · register 18.’ Pell files by destination, not by parcel status.
Register strip: slot 8 holds entries 15–16; slot 9 holds 17–18; slot 10 holds 19–20.
June’s own crossword is in the jail pile. A marked square posted through cell two reaches the prisoner without going over the radio.

stages.prompt: Trace the key and the private question.

board.wrong_text: Pell checks the carbon. “Destination first. Then the printed register strip. Then the prisoner’s own post.”

hints: Pell files by where a thing is going, not by what happened to it.
The register strip prints entry 18 beside slot 9; there is nothing to calculate.
Jail drawer, slot 9, then post June’s marked crossword through cell two.
lines: c6_jail.mail.01

lines.new: steve|June’s own crossword is in the jail pile. I’ll circle one square and post it through her slot.

lines: steve|Twenty-three across, where it crosses eight down. Only the woman in cell two will see that square.
steve|Then I’ll call the Sheriff on the desk radio. Both Junes get the same question.
mail.finding: steve|The key was in the Jail drawer, slot 9, where entries 17 and 18 share a slot. And on June’s crossword I circled the square where 23 Across crosses 8 Down. Only the woman in cell two will see it.

crossword.title: The two Junes
crossword.goal: Check Iris’s story: which June is locked in cell two, and which one is out on the harbor?
crossword.background: June’s rule: memories can’t prove who you are, so you check the paperwork. Iris says the crew scanned June at the safe house. Her copy runs the office, and the real June has been locked in cell two since Friday. Steve posted June’s crossword, with one square circled, into cell two and nowhere else. Whoever is in that cell has seen it. Anyone else has to guess.

lead.new: calder|Mercer. That woman in cell two is a copy. Don’t you dare let her out.
lead.direction: over the front-desk radio, from the harbor

lead.new: calder|Check my paperwork, Mercer. I taught you that.

lead: steve|I’ll ask them both which letter I circled today. Only one of them has seen it.
crossword.prompt: The June in cell two answers on a slip of paper. The June on the radio answers out loud. What should Steve ask about the square he personally circled, and whose answer should he accept?
crossword.instruction: Ask both Junes only: “Which letter did I circle?” Keep the crossing to yourself. Use Steve’s notebook to check their answers. 23 Across, ‘beyond imitation’, is INIMITABLE, shown as I _ I _ I _ A _ L _. Its first, second and last blanks cross 3 Down, 8 Down and 12 Down.

rows.label: Privately check the crossing Steve circled
rows.feedback: I wrote the crossing in my notebook when I slipped the paper into the cell. Don't read those numbers over the radio.

rows.label: Accept the June who says
rows.feedback: Write INIMITABLE across the pattern. Count the blanks, not the printed letters, to find the marked crossing.

hints: Steve said which square he circled when he found the key. His notebook has it too.
Write INIMITABLE under the blanks, one letter at a time.
Find the blank that crosses the down clue Steve chose, and read the letter there.
lines: steve|Radio June said T. Close. Wrong.

lines.text: Twenty-three across. Inimitable. Unlike my colleague on the radio.

lines: c6_jail.crossword.02

lines.new: calder|Stay right there, Mercer. I’m on my way in.
calder|She knows my files. She doesn’t know me. Back door, Mercer.
steve|Pell held the back door. When her patrol car pulled up out front, we were already behind Gus’s bakery.

crossword.finding: steve|The June in cell two had my crossword in her hand: the M where 23 Across crosses 8 Down. The June on the radio guessed a T, so she has never been near that cell. Iris was right. I unlocked cell two, and we left by the back before her copy reached the front.

recap: steve|June is out of her cell. Her copy knows I was there, and that I let June out. Pell chose a beagle over his orders.
steve|Five fugitives and a beagle. We needed a car nobody would look for.
steve|Stephen and Iris were waiting behind Gus’s bakery next door, where nobody would see our faces.

outro.direction: at the bakery loading door, holding out the keys to a van with a giant croissant on its roof

outro: steve|Iris. The ring in my sock drawer. Did Nora ever find it?
iris|A copy who stops going below starts to forget. Nora’s memories go first.

outro.new: steve|By dark the posters were back up, with a new charge from Rook’s copy: Steve Mercer, fled federal custody. June’s copy knew who had opened cell two.

lines: steve|How is Biscuit doing these days?
pell|She eats at seven and at five. She prefers the blue bowl. I am not yet sure she prefers me.
pell|I am working on it. I have learned to scratch behind her left ear.
steve|Do you like the mail route?
pell|Dale’s route has two hundred and twelve stops. Dale liked eleven of them.
pell|I have started to like a twelfth. Carmen gives me a churro at La Marea. The real Dale never stopped there.
steve|What is Dale like? The real one.
pell|He complains about the rain, the dogs and the government. In that order.
pell|I have his memories, but not his complaints. I find I do not miss them.

i2_nora.when: Monday night, inside the Long Patience
i2_nora.coach: You are Nora, awake on the ship. Organize the others at the pods first, then lure the guard into the north wash shaft to clear the aisle.
i2_nora.objective: Organize the pods, draw the guard off the aisle, open the deeper rows and leave Steve a message.
notes: In the Iris chapter, Iris tells Steve how she set this wake: on Sunday night the crew retook her for a reset and left her on a laundry cart in the Gallery, and she set a slow wake on three beds before riding out with the wash. This interlude begins when the slow cycle finishes Monday night.
The lids remain shut while the beds support Nora, Lyle and Dale. They open only after all three breathe independently.
This wake is reversible and leaves the mirror links active. The crew can put Nora back under; Iris’s permanent link-break remains a Chapter 9 choice.

Organize the three sleepers at the pods FIRST (jobs), then use Lyle’s wash-chute jam to lure the guard through the north archway where the bulkhead seals behind him (patrol), then cross the genuinely empty aisle to the pump and intercom.
Row Zero’s enormous eye under the frost is painted in stills/i2_nora-row-zero.webp.
Nora plays this interlude, so her small talk is with Dale and Lyle, the two sleepers awake beside her.
context: nora|I woke up in amber light, in a bed I didn’t choose, in a hall that went on forever.
nora|The bed panel said Monday, November fifth. That was how I learned five months had passed.
nora|I was frightened for about a minute. Then I did what I do at any party where nobody knows each other. I started learning names.

intro.new: nora|The glass stayed shut while three blue strips counted our breaths. The beds did the work until each of us could breathe alone.
nora|Only then did the latches release. WAKE COMPLETE, the panel said. MIRROR LINK ACTIVE.

jobs.title: Plan at the pods
jobs.goal: Assign each awake sleeper to the role they know before moving on the guard.
jobs.background: Three sleepers are awake behind the open pods while a guard watches the Gallery aisle: Nora, the real Lyle Boone and a grumpy mail carrier named Dale.
lead: nora|Everybody’s good at something. Even Dale.
lyle|That north wash chute by the arch jams if you trip the return latch. I can pull it when you say go.
dale|Thirty years on a mail route. Put me on lookout and I’ll log every row and pod number in this place.
jobs.prompt: Who trips the north wash chute, who keeps lookout and logs the rows, and who handles the water pumps?

board.instruction: Give each person the role that fits what they already know how to do.
evidence: Lyle knows how to trip the sticking north wash-chute latch beside the archway.
Dale has spent thirty years memorizing routes and addresses and can log every row on lookout.
Nora is an aquarium engineer who can read the Gallery water circulation gauges.
To reach the pump and intercom across the hall, someone has to jam the north wash chute while another keeps lookout by the pods.

stages.prompt: Put one name on each role.
slots: Who trips the north wash chute to draw the guard off?
Who keeps lookout and logs every row number?
Who works the Gallery circulation pump?

board.wrong_text: Nora shakes her head. Match each person to the skill they just offered.

hints: Each skill matches what each person just offered at the pods.
Lyle handles the mechanical chute latch; Dale tracks routes and numbers; Nora knows pumps.
Lyle trips the north wash chute, Dale keeps lookout and maps the rows, and Nora takes the circulation pump.

lines.text: I’ll trip the wash chute and hold the pods while you cross.

lines: i2_nora.jobs.02
i2_nora.jobs.03
jobs.finding: nora|Lyle trips the north wash chute to draw the guard off. Dale keeps lookout and maps the rows. I take the pumps. Water is the one thing on this ship I understand.

patrol.title: North wash chute
patrol.goal: Lure the guard off the Gallery aisle so the north bulkhead seals behind him.
patrol.background: A Veyri guard stands watch at the north archway, blocking the aisle to the circulation pump and intercom. Beside the arch is the service wash chute that leads into the north laundry shaft.
lead: nora|He never leaves the aisle for a shift bell, and a pod warning brings him straight to us.
nora|Only a north wash-chute jam pulls him through that archway, and the bulkhead locks behind him for a six-minute wash clear.
patrol.prompt: Which alert draws the guard out of the Gallery, and what keeps the aisle clear while Nora works?
patrol.instruction: Check the Gallery service slate. A shift bell makes the guard check the hall without leaving his post. A pod-lid warning brings him directly to Row Nine’s open beds. A north wash-chute jam pulls him through the archway into the laundry shaft, where the brass bulkhead seals automatically for a six-minute wash clear.

rows.label: Trigger to pull the guard off post
rows.feedback: A shift bell keeps him in the hall, and a pod warning sends him right to our open beds. Which alert pulls him into the north shaft?

rows.label: What keeps the aisle clear while Nora works
rows.feedback: Outrunning him across an open glass hall won't keep him away while I work the pump. What seals him out of the Gallery?
options: Sprinting past him down the aisle
The north bulkhead locking behind him for the wash clear

hints: Rule out any alert that leaves the guard in the Gallery or brings him to the pods.
Read what happens to the north archway door once the guard enters the laundry shaft.
Trip the north wash-chute jam so the guard steps into the shaft and the bulkhead locks behind him for six minutes.

lines.text: There goes the chute alarm. He’s through the archway, and the bulkhead locked behind him. The aisle is ours.

patrol.finding: nora|The jammed wash chute pulled the guard into the north shaft and locked the bulkhead behind him for six minutes. Lyle and Dale are watching the pods, and the Gallery aisle is clear.

pump.title: Gallery circulation
pump.goal: Lower the pressure at the deeper Gallery hatch without starving the beds.
pump.background: Nora knows pumps from the aquarium. The Gallery runs on water too: one circuit feeds the beds, another returns it. Opening the deeper Gallery hatch with return pressure high would trip the hall alarm.
lead: nora|Three service branches. Let’s see what each one does.
nora|The top dial reads an empty wash line. Ignore it. Watch the return and the bed flow.
nora|Bed flow has to stay at three or more. The return has to drop below three.
pump.prompt: Which branch should Nora open, and which dial should she trust?
pump.instruction: Pick the branch that keeps bed flow at 3 or more and drops RETURN below 3. Amber: upper 4, RETURN 7, bed flow 4. Blue: upper 1, RETURN 2, bed flow 4. White: upper 3, RETURN 2, bed flow 1.

rows.label: Branch
rows.feedback: I can't trade the sleepers' flow for a lower return. Check both readings on the same branch.

rows.label: Dial to trust
rows.feedback: The upper dial is on an empty line. Check the pressure coming back from the beds.

hints: The upper dial reads an empty line. Watch the RETURN dial and the bed flow.
Amber keeps the beds fed but the RETURN is high. White drops the pressure but starves the beds.
Ignore the upper dial. You need bed flow of 3 or more and a RETURN below 3. Only one trial does both.
lines: i2_nora.pump.01
pump.finding: nora|The Blue branch keeps the beds at 4 and drops the RETURN to 2. The hatch can open, and nobody’s breathing changes.

message.title: Gallery intercom
message.goal: Leave a private message for Steve before scouting the deeper rows.
message.background: The Gallery intercom has three message slots. If Steve comes at all, he might come on any watch. Only Steve should hear what Nora says.
lead: nora|If he comes. When he comes. He’ll come.
message.prompt: Where should Nora store her message for Steve?
options: Slot A: broadcasts to every bed now
Slot B: queued on Bed Three’s terminal for PLAY
Slot C: clears when the watch changes

wrong.0: Every sleeper, and every guard, would hear it right now.
wrong.2: It would be gone by the next watch, and Steve could come on any watch.

hints: Who should hear it, and when?
It has to survive a change of watch, and only Steve should start it.
Rule out the slot every guard would hear and the slot that clears at the change of watch.
lines: i2_nora.message.01
message.finding: nora|My message for Steve is queued in Slot B on Bed Three’s terminal. It will wait for him.

recap: nora|I know every name in my row now. I have a route, a crew and a pump that behaves.
nora|I counted thirteen months of silence before they took me. Five more went by while I slept. I still want to hear what he has to say.

outro.new: nora|Under the frost, something opened one enormous eye. It looked at me. Then it closed again.

lines: nora|How are you feeling, Dale?
dale|Cold, stiff and starving. If this is a hospital, the food is terrible.
nora|There isn’t any food here, Dale.
dale|That is exactly my point, Nora.
dale|Who is feeding June Calder’s beagle? I carry biscuits in my bag for her every morning.
nora|I’m sure somebody is looking after Biscuit.
dale|Somebody had better be. She sulks at anyone who forgets.
dale|Left at the pipes, right at the cold one, straight past the humming wall.
nora|You really did learn the whole route.
dale|Mail carriers never forget a route, Nora. We only forget birthdays.
lyle|My boys have a game on Saturday. I’ve missed most of their games this year.
nora|Then you’ll make the next one, Lyle.
lyle|Every single one, when I get out of here. I swear it.
lyle|I should be at work. Somebody must be covering my shifts.
nora|I think somebody probably is, Lyle.
lyle|Then I hope he’s nicer to Steve Mercer than I was.
